overlaps.locator: Main article, Results, paragraph beginning “We applied several strategies”; Supplementary Information S3.5, p. 8
overlaps.quote: “Our final dataset included 56,086 unique nucleotide sequences coding for 51,715 different protein sequences.”; “The final dataset consisted of 56,086 unique nucleotide genotypes and 51,715 unique amino acid genotypes.”
overlaps.definition_quote: “We excluded genotypes containing insertions, deletions or stop codons, and grouped barcodes with the same nucleotide or amino acid genotypes. The final dataset consisted of 56,086 unique nucleotide genotypes and 51,715 unique amino acid genotypes.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper counts all measured unique amino-acid genotypes after its stated exclusions. GraphFLA’s built-graph n_configs omits isolated genotypes with no observed one-amino-acid neighbor. The paper also states that the sampled fraction is tiny for sequences with more than two mutations, so the input is a sparse local sample.

input.preprocessing: Removed rows with a stop symbol in aaMutations per Supplementary Information S3.5; reconstructed protein strings from the archived reference and amino-acid substitutions; used medianBrightness unchanged.

overlaps.reason: GraphFLA retained 17,604 vertices and 35,092 directed improving edges; its build warning reports 34,111 isolated configurations removed. The retained-graph count is not the paper’s count of measured genotypes.

overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper reports unique nucleotide genotypes, while GraphFLA n_configs is the number of vertices retained after graph construction and isolated-node removal. In addition, the archive mutation list conflicts with its archived reference at one coordinate for 915 filtered input rows; no coordinate or allele correction was justified by the paper.

input.preprocessing: Filtered out rows marked with a stop in aaMutations per Supplementary Information S3.5. Reconstruction from nMutations against the archived reference found reference-allele conflicts; no corrections or imputation applied.

overlaps.reason: The attempted reconstruction found 915 reference-allele conflicts, all at position 191: the mutation strings state reference A while the archived reference has G. The DNALandscape build was not run rather than applying an unsupported repair.

overlaps.locator: Main article, Results, paragraph beginning “In a unidimensional landscape”
overlaps.quote: “This simplest, non-epistatic model explained only 70% of the initial sample variance (σ²=1.12 and σ²=0.34 before and after the application of the model, respectively).”
overlaps.definition_quote: “We used multiple regression considering a non-epistatic fitness function whereby log-fluorescence, F, is equal to the linear predictor, the fitness potential, p, such that F=f(p)=p.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: The additive regression is conceptually close to GraphFLA order-1 polynomial regression, but GraphFLA fits only the 17,604 vertices retained after isolate removal; the paper’s variance statistic is for its full measured genotype sample.

input.preprocessing: Paper-stated final amino-acid genotype set after stop/indel exclusions; medianBrightness used unchanged; GraphFLA subsequently removed isolated nodes.

overlaps.graphfla_call: A.higher_order_epistasis(ls, order=1, verbose=False) after ProteinLandscape().build_from_data(..., epsilon=0)
overlaps.reason: GraphFLA order-1 R² on the pruned graph is 0.8700741822810955, versus the printed 70%. This comparison changes the fitted observations through graph pruning and is not a reproduction of the full-sample fit.

overlaps.paper_value: up to 30% of genotypes with multiple mutations, varying with mutation count
overlaps.locator: Main article, Results, paragraph beginning “Interaction of deleterious mutations can manifest in positive epistasis”
overlaps.quote: “Negative epistasis affected up to 30% of all genotypes, depending on the number of mutations.”
overlaps.definition_quote: “We defined strong epistasis as |e| > 0.7, or as cases where the observed fluorescence differed from the expected by at least fivefold, with a false discovery rate of < 1%.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper counts genotype-level strong negative epistasis using a clipped additive expectation and mutation-count strata. GraphFLA classify_epistasis partitions four-node motif instances into motif classes.

input.preprocessing: Not run; paper’s class denominator and strong-epistasis rule do not match GraphFLA motif fractions.

overlaps.reason: A genotype-level prevalence is not the proportion of four-node motifs in a GraphFLA graph.

overlaps.locator: Supplementary Information S4.1 “Single mutant analysis,” p. 8
overlaps.quote: “Sequences with log-fluorescence < 3.0 have light intensity less than wild-type by 10^{3.72-3.0} ≈ 5 times (Figure 2a). 9.4% of genotypes had such low intensity, which we considered non-fluorescent.”
overlaps.definition_quote: “Sequences with log-fluorescence < 3.0 … 9.4% of genotypes had such low intensity, which we considered non-fluorescent.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: This is a thresholded fraction of genotypes, not one of GraphFLA fitness_distribution’s unitless shape statistics; the paper’s denominator also includes the full sample rather than the pruned graph.

input.preprocessing: Not run; no matching threshold-fraction output in GraphFLA fitness_distribution.

overlaps.graphfla_call: not run; GraphFLA fitness_distribution has no threshold-fraction field
overlaps.reason: The named GraphFLA metric reports distribution moments and ratios, not the paper’s fraction below log-fluorescence 3.0.

overlaps.locator: Supplementary Information S4.7 “Path accessibility on the fitness landscapes,” p. 14
overlaps.quote: “The lower bound fraction of inaccessible paths was 0/596,228,074 (0%), 1,201,621/70,670,872 (1.7%), 13,324/202,308 (6.6%) and 6/174 (3.4%) for paths 1.2 (blue) 1.6 (orange), 2.0 (red), and 2.4 (purple), substitutions away from the wildtype, respectively (colour-coded with Supplementary Fig. 3).”
overlaps.definition_quote: “We considered a path as accessible if all of the three intermediate genotypes were neutral or advantageous, that is conferred fluorescence at least as high as points at the ends of the path.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper counts shortest paths between pairs of fluorescent genotypes at a specified distance from wild type. GraphFLA global_optima_accessibility measures access to a global optimum in its directed improving-edge graph.
overlaps.reason: The published path groups are not paths to a global optimum, so the GraphFLA output would not be a reproduction.

verdict_reason: The paper prints unique genotype counts, additive and nonlinear variance fits, a genotype-level epistasis prevalence, a thresholded fluorescence fraction, and lower-bound path fractions. GraphFLA reproduced none exactly: the protein graph count and order-1 R² differ after isolate pruning, nucleotide reconstruction is blocked by reference conflicts, and the remaining targets use different definitions. No local-optimum count is stated.
